description.narrative:
GESTERRA var ett program som implementerades mellan 2013 och 2019, med syfte att etablera väl utformat, reglerat, transparent och implementerat markförvaltningssystem baserad på inkluderande ekonomisk och social utveckling. Programmet hade två huvudkomponenter: (i) markförvaltning som främjar en integrerad vision av markadministration och styrning, och (ii) markförvaltningstjänster och skapandet av landstadsregistret.
Programmet fokuserade på institutionell kapacitetsuppbyggnad, systemutveckling och decentraliserad utrullning av markförvaltningssystemet. Genom DINAT, det nationella fastighetsregistret i Moçambique ('Direcção Nacional de Terras), skulle Moçambiques regering kunna leda markförvaltningsprocessen och spela en kritisk och konstruktiv roll i markförvaltningen, med förbättrad kommunikation och upprätthållande av tekniska normer och standarder för markförvaltning, samt övervakning och kvalitetskontroll.

GESTERRA was a programme that was implemented between 2013 and 2019, aiming to establish a well-designed and regulated, transparent and implemented land governance system as the basis for inclusive social and economic development. The programme had two main components: (i) Land governance for an integrated vision of land management and land administration, and (ii) Land administration services and building of the National Land Cadastre.
The programme focused on institutional capacity building, system development, and de-centralised roll-out of the land administration system. Through DINAT, the National Land Registry in Mozambique (the 'Direcção Nacional de Terras), the Government of Mozambique would be able to lead the land management process and play a critical and constructive role in land governance, with improved communication and enforcement of technical norms and standards for land administration, as well as monitoring and quality control.

GESTERRA was a programme that was implemented between 2013 and 2019, aiming to establish a well-designed and regulated, transparent and implemented land governance system as the basis for inclusive social and economic development. The programme had two main components: (i) Land governance for an integrated vision of land management and land administration, and (ii) Land administration services and building of the National Land Cadastre.
The programme focused on institutional capacity building, system development, and de-centralised roll-out of the land administration system. Through DINAT, the National Land Registry in Mozambique (the 'Direcção Nacional de Terras), the Government of Mozambique would be able to lead the land management process and play a critical and constructive role in land governance, with improved communication and enforcement of technical norms and standards for land administration, as well as monitoring and quality control.

Overall, the programme has made remarkable progress in terms of land administration translated into number of regularisation of occupations. The methodology guidelines for Community delimitation and Regularisation of land occupations were improved by the addition of social and environmental safeguards. Training was carried out and the registration time per plot reduced considerably, but the design of a sustainable model for land management was still to be completed at the end of the program period.
The programme has also been the key success factor in the implementation of government programme so-called "Terra Segura" aiming land occupation registry and regularization by allowing faster and better quality issuance of land utilization titles through digital system.
The institutional restructuring in 2015 reinforced DINAT with new departments and sections and strengthened the land inspection role. In this regard DINAT trained its staff (47 staff from Maputo as well as provincial offices) on fit-for-purpose methodology for systematic registration of land occupation as well as simplified methodology for digital land utilization rights (RDUAT). DINAT also benefited from the institutional capacity building efforts in the areas of financial management, land management and administration and rehabilitation of infrastructure. However, the restructering also reduced the administrative autonomy and had serious implications in terms of human resources (freeze on government hiring of new staff). This lack of technical staff meant that technical assistance provided was utilised to implement the programme rather than to transfer skills, and capacity building efforts were not sustainable.
Through 20 monitoring missions, a total of 243 606 of land plots were revised, of which 126 929 were conformed with quality criteria and registered in SIGIT (see below). From these revised land plots, a total of 122 408 RDUAT (land titles) were issued, however only 87 199 RDUAT were eventually handed to the respective beneficiaries.
The programmes main achievement was the 2016 SiGIT Masterplan (Sistema de Gestão e Informação de Terras) , a Land Information and Management System. SiGIT included the preparation of a masterplan, development, testing and roll-out of the system in all provinces, establishment of a service desk at DINAT, capacity building at central and provincial level, transfer of analogue data, rehabilitation of infrastructure at national and provincial level and establishment of SiGIT laboratories. SiGIT has led to reduced processing time and reduced the risks for overlaps of demarcations. A number of challenges still remained though such as lack of technical capacity to maintain the system, problems with Internet and power supply, and need for ongoing system development.
Consultative Land Forums (Fórum de Consultas sobre Terras FCT) was realised in Gaza, Tete and Cabo Delgado provinces with participation from civil society, private sector, government and other stakeholders. One result was the revised land policy and land legislation. The FCT secretariat however remained embedded within DINAT, with limited resources and autonomy and was (temporarily) discontinued in 2018.
An exchange of information between DINAT and the National Directorate of Land Planning and Resettlement (DINAPOT) allowed the provision of 10 land development plans of the selected districts for preparation, selection, planning and implementation of RDUATs.
The strategic gender guidelines were revised and contributed to the national land inspection campaign as well as community delimitation and regularisations of land occupations processes. However, there was very limited progress in systematic gender mainstreaming and issues such as polygamous marriages, co-registration of land and registration of land in the name of the wife remained important challenges.
The study on land tax collection system revision funded by World bank was concluded and the effort was to disseminate the findings and recommendations. Although the study results were useful for increasing the revenue from land tax, the problems of increase the land tax base are structural and needed to be tackled taking into consideration the proposals that are part of strategy for land sector reform which is more comprehensive.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
